milestone.title: M159/M160/M161 perf AC threshold re-spec — measure what actually drops (incremental + warm-cache + cold-3rd-run)

intent.outcome: After this ships, every performance AC across M159 (cold-nextest ≥30 s drop, actual 17.4 s), M160 (warm-cache ≥50 % drop, actual 19.2 %), and M161 (oracle split ≥1 min cold drop, actual +4.21 s i.e. zero) has a measurable, hardware-portable threshold. The AC descriptions match the actual drop (or are re-scoped to where the win actually lives — incremental rebuild, warm-cache, shared CI backend). The force-bypassed markers on verification.evidence are cleared via M165's amend surface. A regression test asserts that every AC verification command either (a) executes a measurement and parses the numeric threshold, or (b) is explicitly marked manual-only with a documented re-measurement schedule.

problem.description: Three performance milestones (M159, M160, M161) shipped with quantitative AC thresholds that were set without local measurement (Entry 24, Entry 26, Entry 27 in mp-dogfood-log.md). The AC verifier (crates/mp/src/ac_verify.rs) is exit-code-only — it doesn't parse numeric thresholds — so the ACs classify as `passed` despite the actual drop being far below target. The pattern is consistent across all three: AC description overshoots, the milestone ships with a `[force-bypassed: ...]` marker on verification.evidence, the closure path is documented in mp-dogfood-log.md and B-83 / Entry 24/26/27, but the AC text was never rewritten to match reality. The same structural issue will recur in any future perf milestone unless the AC verifier learns to parse numeric thresholds OR the spec-authoring convention requires local measurement before setting a quantitative threshold.

in_scope: M159 AC-01 re-spec (Entry 24): rewrite the AC-01 description's quantitative threshold from '≥30 s cold nextest drop' to the measured '≥15 s cold nextest drop (3-run mean 17.4 s, range 17.7–17.9 s on this Mac, documented in mp-dogfood-log.md entry 24)'. Update F-01 in M159 to 'fixed' with the new threshold and re-publish the evidence field. Clear the `[force-bypassed: ...]` marker via `mp milestone update 159 --verification <new evidence>` (M165 surface).

M160 AC-01 re-spec (Entry 26): rewrite the AC-01 description's quantitative threshold from '≥50 % drop' to '≥15 % drop on a local warm-cache 3rd run' — the local proxy measure. Add a sibling AC AC-01b that defers the CI shared-backend measurement to the first PR run and records the actual drop in the AC's evidence field once the workflow has run. Document the local-vs-CI gap in the AC description. Clear the `[force-bypassed: ...]` marker.

M161 AC-04 re-spec (Entry 27): rewrite AC-04 from '≥1 min cold wall-clock drop' to 'incremental mp-src-edit re-link time drops by ≥5 s (post-oracle-split; jsonschema confined to mp-oracle's 2 test binaries)'. The actual win lives in incremental rebuilds, not cold builds. Update the AC verification command to: `cargo clean && cargo build -p mp && /usr/bin/time -p bash -c 'touch crates/mp/src/lib.rs && cargo nextest run -p mp --no-fail-fast'` and assert wall-clock ≤ pre-split baseline. Clear the `[force-bypassed: ...]` marker.

Add a new helper `crates/mp/src/perf_measure.rs` that exposes a measurement macro `mp_measure!(label, command) -> {mean_s, stddev_s, runs}` running the command N=3 times with /usr/bin/time -p, returning a structured record. The M159/M160/M161 ACs use this macro in their verification fields instead of `make test`. The macro parses numeric output and pins the threshold; if the threshold is not met, the AC classifies as `failed` rather than `passed` (close the exit-code-only gap).

Add crates/mp/tests/perf_ac_threshold_reality_check.rs that walks every milestone on disk, reads each AC's `verification` field, and flags any string matching `(≥|>=|>=?).*?(s|%|x|min|sec)` without an `mp_measure!` wrapper or `manual:` prefix as a 'perf AC without numeric gate' warning. Fail the test if the count of perf ACs without gates exceeds 0.

Document the new convention in docs/concepts/03 - Planning Methodology/PERF-ACS.md (new file): 'every quantitative AC must use mp_measure! and the threshold must be measured locally before authoring'. Cross-link from GROOMING.md.
After each AC rewrite, clear the corresponding `[force-bypassed: ...]` marker via `mp milestone update`.
out_of_scope: Actually shipping the cold-30s / warm-50% / cold-1min AC drops (mold, sccache, split-debuginfo) — that's a separate track if the team wants to invest; M176 re-specs the ACs, doesn't deliver the perf.
Touching the AC verifier's exit-code-only classification in other dimensions — the perf_measure macro is the focused fix.
Re-running the bulk lifecycle migration or any plan-zone data move.
Touching M162 / M165 / M167 AC thresholds — they don't carry quantitative perf claims and aren't subject to the same pattern.
Adding a wall-clock CI gate — CI gates that fail PRs on threshold miss are out of M176 scope; M176 only fixes the local reality-check.
Auto-correcting future perf-AC drift — the perf_measure macro + test pin is the preventive measure; an enforcement rule at author-time is a separate work item.
